title: Oxidation, Reduction & Electrochemistry

notes.heading: 1. Oxidation Numbers, Peroxide Exceptions & Redox n-Factors
notes.proseLatex: Oxidation is electron loss (oxidation number increases; reducing agent) and reduction is electron gain (oxidation number decreases; oxidizing agent). Watch peroxide ($\text{O} = -1$) traps: $\text{CrO}_5$ ('butterfly' with two peroxo rings) has $\text{Cr} = +6$ (NOT $+10$!), and Caro's acid $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$ has $\text{S} = +6$ (NOT $+8$!). For $\text{KMnO}_4$, $n$-factor is $5$ in acidic ($\text{MnO}_4^- \to \text{Mn}^{2+}$), $3$ in neutral/faintly alkaline ($\to \text{MnO}_2$), and $1$ in strongly alkaline ($\to \text{MnO}_4^{2-}$).

notes.heading: 2. Faraday's Laws of Electrolysis & Conductance
notes.proseLatex: One Faraday $F = N_A e \approx 96{,}500\text{ C/mol}$ deposits exactly $1$ gram-equivalent of ANY substance! Faraday's 1st law gives deposited mass $w = ZIt = \frac{E\,I\,t}{96500}$, and for cells in series (equal charge $Q$), Faraday's 2nd law gives $\frac{w_1}{w_2} = \frac{E_1}{E_2}$. Upon dilution, specific conductivity $\kappa$ DECREASES (fewer ions per $\text{cm}^3$), whereas molar conductivity $\Lambda_m = \frac{1000\kappa}{M}$ INCREASES (Kohlrausch's law $\Lambda_m^\circ = \nu_+\lambda_+^\circ + \nu_-\lambda_-^\circ$).

notes.heading: 3. Galvanic Cells, Nernst Equation & Gibbs Free Energy
notes.proseLatex: Oxidation ALWAYS occurs at the ANODE and reduction at the CATHODE (LOAN: Left, Oxidation, Anode, Negative in galvanic cells; in electrolytic cells, anode is positive!). Standard cell EMF is $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}}$, spontaneity requires $\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ_{\text{cell}} < 0$, and at $298\text{ K}$ the Nernst equation reads $E_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cell}} - \frac{0.0591}{n}\log_{10} Q$.

wbjeebTraps: $E^\circ$ is an INTENSIVE property: multiplying a half-reaction by $2$ never multiplies $E^\circ$ — when combining two half-reactions into a third half-reaction, add $\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ$ ($n_3 E_3^\circ = n_1 E_1^\circ + n_2 E_2^\circ$), NEVER $E^\circ$ directly!
Maximum oxidation number of an element never exceeds its group valence electrons ($\text{Cr}=+6$ in $\text{CrO}_5$, $\text{S}=+6$ in $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$).
Specific conductivity $\kappa$ FALLS on dilution, while molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ RISES on dilution!

conceptPrimer.heading: Oxidation Numbers and the Peroxide Traps
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Oxidation = electron loss (oxidation number rises; the species is the reducing agent); reduction = electron gain (ON falls; oxidizing agent). Oxygen is $-2$ EXCEPT in peroxides where it is $-1$ — that single exception defuses JELET's favourite traps: in $\text{CrO}_5$ (butterfly, two peroxo rings) chromium is $+6$, NOT $+10$; in Caro's acid $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$ sulphur is $+6$, NOT $+8$. Micro-check: $\text{CrO}_5$ carries four peroxo O ($-1$ each) and one oxo O ($-2$): $x + 4(-1) + (-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6$.

conceptPrimer.heading: n-Factors and Equivalent Weights
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: The $n$-factor is electrons transferred per formula unit, and it depends on the MEDIUM. For $\text{KMnO}_4$: $n_f = 5$ in acid ($\text{Mn}^{2+}$), $3$ in neutral/faintly alkaline ($\text{MnO}_2$), $1$ in strongly alkaline ($\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$); for acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$, $n_f = 6$ (two Cr, $+6 \to +3$ each). Equivalent weight $E = \frac{M}{n_f}$. Micro-check: $E(\text{KMnO}_4)$ in acid $= \frac{158}{5} = 31.6$; in neutral medium $\frac{158}{3} \approx 52.7$ — three different answers from one salt.

conceptPrimer.heading: Faraday's Laws of Electrolysis
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: One faraday $F = 96500\ \text{C}$ deposits ONE gram-equivalent of any substance. First law: $w = \frac{E\,I\,t}{96500} = \frac{M\,I\,t}{n_f\,F}$. Second law (cells in series, equal charge): $\frac{w_1}{w_2} = \frac{E_1}{E_2}$. Always compute charge first: $Q = It$, then moles of electrons $= \frac{Q}{F}$. Micro-check: $0.5\ \text{F}$ through $\text{AgNO}_3$: $w = 108 \times 0.5 = 54\ \text{g}$ of Ag ($n_f = 1$).

conceptPrimer.heading: Conductance: κ Falls, Λm Rises
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Specific conductivity $\kappa$ counts ions per $\text{cm}^3$, so DILUTION lowers it. Molar conductivity $\Lambda_m = \frac{1000\,\kappa}{M}$ counts conducting power per mole — dilution increases it (ions travel farther apart, less mutual blocking). Kohlrausch's law adds limiting values independently: $\Lambda_m^\circ = \nu_+\lambda_+^\circ + \nu_-\lambda_-^\circ$. Micro-check: dilute 10-fold: $\kappa$ drops, $M$ drops 10-fold faster than $\kappa$, so $\Lambda_m = \frac{1000\kappa}{M}$ climbs.

conceptPrimer.heading: Galvanic Cells: Anatomy and Standard EMF
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: LOAN for galvanic cells: Left electrode — Oxidation — Anode — Negative. (In electrolytic cells the anode is POSITIVE.) Standard EMF uses both half-cells as reduction potentials: $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}}$, and spontaneity links everything to Gibbs: $\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ_{\text{cell}} < 0$. Micro-check: Daniell: $E^\circ = 0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10\ \text{V}$, so $\Delta G^\circ = -2 \times 96500 \times 1.10 \approx -212\ \text{kJ/mol}$ — spontaneous.

conceptPrimer.heading: Nernst Equation and the Cell–Equilibrium Bridge
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: At $298\ \text{K}$: $E_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cell}} - \frac{0.0591}{n}\log_{10} Q$ (reaction quotient $Q$). The cell dies at equilibrium: $E = 0$ exactly when $Q = K_{\text{eq}}$, giving $\log K_{\text{eq}} = \frac{nE^\circ}{0.0591}$. Remember $n$ — electrons in the BALANCED overall reaction. Micro-check: Daniell with $[\text{Cu}^{2+}] = 0.1$, $[\text{Zn}^{2+}] = 1$: $Q = 10$, $E = 1.10 - \frac{0.0591}{2} \times 1 \approx 1.07\ \text{V}$.

keyDefinitions.definition: Oxidation: loss of electrons, ON increases. Reduction: gain of electrons, ON decreases.
Oxidizing agent gains electrons (is reduced); reducing agent loses electrons (is oxidized).
Formal charge an atom would carry if every bond were fully ionic.
Electrons transferred per formula unit; $E = M/n_f$. Depends on the reaction medium.
$F = N_A e \approx 96500\ \text{C/mol}$ — charge of one mole of electrons.
Conductance of $1\ \text{cm}^3$ of solution; falls on dilution (fewer ions per cm³).
$\Lambda_m = 1000\kappa/M$; conducting power per mole; rises on dilution.
At infinite dilution each ion contributes its own limiting molar conductivity, independent of the counter-ion.
Oxidation always at the anode, reduction at the cathode — polarity flips between galvanic (anode −) and electrolytic (anode +).

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: The oxidation state of Cr in $\text{CrO}_5$ is:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Four peroxo O at $-1$ and one oxo O at $-2$: $x - 4 - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6$. Chromium never exceeds its group valence $+6$ — $+10$ is the classic trap.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: The oxidation state of S in Caro's acid $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$ is:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Structure has one $\mathrm{-O-O-}$ bridge (2 peroxo O at $-1$ each) plus three oxo O at $-2$: $2(+1) + x + 3(-2) + 2(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6$. Sulphur cannot exceed $+6$.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: Equivalent weight of $\text{KMnO}_4$ ($M = 158$) in NEUTRAL medium:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Neutral medium: $n_f = 3$ ($\text{MnO}_4^- \to \text{MnO}_2$). $E = \frac{158}{3} \approx 52.7$ — NOT $\frac{158}{5} = 31.6$, which is the acidic value.

For the Daniell cell with $[\text{Zn}^{2+}] = 1\ \text{M}$ and $[\text{Cu}^{2+}] = 0.1\ \text{M}$, the cell EMF at $298\ \text{K}$ is:
On dilution, specific conductivity $\kappa$ and molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ respectively:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Fewer ions per $\text{cm}^3$ pull $\kappa$ down; $\Lambda_m = 1000\kappa/M$ rises because $M$ falls faster and ions migrate farther apart.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: Given $\text{Fe}^{3+} + e^- \to \text{Fe}^{2+}$, $E^\circ_1 = 0.77\ \text{V}$ and $\text{Fe}^{2+} + 2e^- \to \text{Fe}$, $E^\circ_2 = -0.44\ \text{V}$, the standard potential of $\text{Fe}^{3+} + 3e^- \to \text{Fe}$ is:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Combine via $\Delta G^\circ$: $n_3E_3^\circ = 1(0.77) + 2(-0.44) = -0.11$, so $E_3^\circ = \frac{-0.11}{3} \approx -0.037\ \text{V} \approx -0.04\ \text{V}$. Adding raw potentials ($0.33$) is the trap — $E^\circ$ is intensive.

memoryHooks: Peroxide O = $-1$: butterflies keep Cr at $+6$ and Caro's S at $+6$.
Medium picks the n-factor: Mn gives $5, 3, 1$ in acid, neutral, base.
One faraday, one gram-equivalent — of ANY substance.
Series cells share charge; masses split by equivalent weights.
κ falls, Λm rises — dilution's seesaw.
LOAN: Left – Oxidation – Anode – Negative (galvanic cells).
$E^\circ$ is intensive: never multiply it; add $\Delta G^\circ$ instead.
$E = 0$ when $Q = K$: the cell flat-lines at equilibrium.
commonMistakes: Assigning Cr $= +10$ in $\text{CrO}_5$ or S $= +8$ in $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$ (counting peroxo O as $-2$).
Using the acidic $n_f = 5$ for $\text{KMnO}_4$ in neutral or alkaline medium.
Multiplying $E^\circ$ by $n$ when scaling a half-reaction.
Swapping anode polarity between galvanic (−) and electrolytic (+) cells.
Using $0.0591$ without dividing by $n$ in the Nernst equation.
Writing $\log K = E^\circ/0.0591$ without the factor $n$.
Reporting $\Delta G^\circ > 0$ for a spontaneous ($E^\circ > 0$) cell.
examChecklist: Assign peroxo O ($-1$) before summing oxidation numbers.
Pick the n-factor by MEDIUM, then $E = M/n_f$.
Start every electrolysis problem with $Q = It$, then moles of $e^- = Q/F$.
In series cells, masses are proportional to equivalent weights only.
Recite κ↓ / Λm↑ on dilution, with the reason.
$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = $ cathode − anode, both as reduction potentials.
Nernst: divide $0.0591$ by $n$; use $Q$ with balanced-stoichiometry exponents.
Combine half-cells through $n_3E_3^\circ = n_1E_1^\circ + n_2E_2^\circ$, never raw $E^\circ$.
$\log K = nE^\circ/0.0591$ bridges cells and equilibria.
Electrolytic cells: anode positive, cathode negative.
